battle.name: 漢摩拉比征服拉爾薩
battle.theater: 美索不達米亞南部拉爾薩
battle.brief: 公元前1763年，巴比倫王漢摩拉比在北方擊破埃什努納與埃蘭、古提的聯軍後轉兵南下，沿幼發拉底河攻向拉爾薩，於沙特卡爾河畔擊潰辛-穆巴里特的軍隊，圍城破垣，毀其沙瑪什神廟，擒其國王而北走，拉爾薩就此滅亡。蘇美爾城邦並立時代就此告終。卡面埃及長矛並未隨軍，陣上刺穿皮甲的是套筒銅矛。

kit.name: 埃及長矛
kit.history: 早王朝時期的長矛，銅或青銅矛頭綁在木杆上。埃及人用它守城垣，後來也用它收復失地。

countries: 拉爾薩之戰是巴比倫與拉爾薩兩方在兩河流域南部的一場王國對城邦的戰爭。巴比倫一方是阿摩拉特王朝的中央集權王國：國王漢摩拉比兼最高統帥，率領以城防常備步兵為骨幹的軍隊，步兵在當時是決定性兵種，射手與標槍兵為輔，輔以小量騎乘傳令與運載；王室的宮廷書記官隨軍記錄戰果，這正是《漢摩拉比編年史》與《巴比倫王表 A》殘卷的來源。巴比倫的軍隊體系建立在南方的城鄉徵發之上：它可以從烏爾、蘇普拉庫姆等城邦調集民夫修築堤防、輸送糧秣，並用「底格里斯河長牆」把北方的蘇巴爾圖（埃什努納）隔在牆外。拉爾薩一方則是蘇美爾城邦的典型軍國：位於幼發拉底河中游支流沙特卡爾河兩岸的拉爾薩城，在辛-穆巴里特治下控制中游的鹽、穀物與航道，軍隊以城邦民兵為主，並得到東方埃蘭與古提聯盟的兵力支援；城神札巴巴與太陽神沙瑪什的神廟構成其祭祀與徵召的合法性，國王須在神廟主持出師儀式，方能召集鄉民與僱傭兵。第三方並非中立：埃什努納、烏爾、伊辛等城邦在巴比倫與拉爾薩之間首鼠兩端，漢摩拉比先在北方拆散聯盟，再南下各個擊破，戰後更把伊辛、蘇普拉庫姆等城直接吞併，使巴比倫的指揮系統第一次深入整個南部平原。
countriesEn: The war for Larsa was fought between a kingdom and a city-state on the southern Mesopotamian alluvial plain. On the Babylonian side stood the centralised Amorite state of the Old Babylonian period. King Hammurabi was himself the supreme commander, and he led an army whose backbone was the standing infantry of the fortified capital, infantry being the decisive arm of the age, with archers and javelin-men in support and a small number of horsemen used for dispatch and for carrying. The palace scribes went with the king and wrote down the results of the campaign, and those texts are precisely the source of the Chronicle of Hammurabi and of the relevant fragment of Babylonian King List A. The Babylonian military system rested on the levy of the cities and countryside of the south: it could draw forced labour from Ur and Suprakum to raise embankments and move grain, and it used the Wall of the Tigris to hold the northern enemy, Subartu, that is Eshnunna, on the far side of a defended line. Larsa, by contrast, was a typical city-state of Sumer. The city stood on both banks of the Shatt al-Kar, a branch of the Euphrates in its middle reach, and under Sin-Muballit it controlled the salt, the grain and the shipping of that stretch of river. Its forces were based on the militia of the city, reinforced by contingents supplied by its allies to the east, the Elamites and the Gutians. The city god Zababa and the temple of Shamash gave its levies and its rituals their legitimacy, and the king had to preside over the departure ceremony in the temple before the countryside could be called out and the mercenaries hired. The third parties were not neutral either. Eshnunna, Ur, Isin and the other cities sat on the fence between Babylon and Larsa; Hammurabi first broke up the alliance in the north, then marched south and picked the cities off one by one, and after the war he annexed Isin and Suprakum outright, so that the Babylonian command system reached, for the first time, across the whole southern plain.
people: 留下姓名的只有兩位君主，卻足以定下這場戰爭的走向。漢摩拉比，阿摩拉特王朝第六代君主，祖父為王朝奠基者薩姆松-阿巴德一世；中等年代學把他的在位定於公元前1792至1750年，短年代學則作前1848至1806年，兩說相差約五十六年，而拉爾薩陷落通常繫於他在位第37年，通行定年為公元前1763年。漢摩拉比並非以蠻力壓倒對手：他的做法是先以底格里斯河長牆與北方的戰役固定北境，再逐次離散拉爾薩的聯盟，最後才傾國力南下；他也把治水與水利工程當作國策，著名的洪水渠開鑿與河道分疏既為農耕，也為行軍與運糧服務，馬里王國的泥板信件（年代與此役相當）記載過巴比倫王對幼發拉底河下游水量與鹽分的干預。拉爾薩王辛-穆巴里特（又作西姆穆巴里特）是拉爾薩的末代君主，也是蘇美爾城邦時代最有作為的統治者之一：他擴張了對幼發拉底河中游的支配，維持與埃蘭的軍事同盟，並曾兩度與巴比倫交兵；此役戰敗後，他帶著城邦的神像與王室財貨退往北方的哈茲班，一般認為在哈布爾河上游一帶，地點至今未能確定。拉爾薩的祭司與文書官在城破時被殺或被擄，城內居民則被拆散分配；漢摩拉比身邊能點名者，除王家書記官外別無可靠記載，這本身就說明這場戰爭的史料幾乎全部來自勝方留下的泥板。
peopleEn: Only two monarchs leave a name, but they are enough to settle the course of the war. Hammurabi, the sixth ruler of the Amorite dynasty, was a grandson of Samsun-Abad I, the founder of the line; the Middle Chronology places his reign between 1792 and 1750 BC and the Short Chronology between 1848 and 1806 BC, the two differing by some fifty-six years, and the fall of Larsa is usually tied to the thirty-seventh year of his reign, conventionally dated to 1763 BC. Hammurabi did not crush his enemy by brute force. His method was to fix the northern frontier first with the Wall of the Tigris and the campaigns beyond it, then to break up Larsa's alliance piece by piece, and only at the end to bring the whole weight of the state south. He also treated the control of water and of hydraulic works as policy: the cutting of flood channels and the diversion of river courses served the fields, the marching columns and the grain convoys alike, and the clay tablets of Mari, whose dates run parallel with this war, record the Babylonian king's interference with the volume and the salt of the lower Euphrates. Sin-Muballit, also written Simmuballut, was the last king of Larsa and among the most capable rulers of the Sumerian city-state age. He extended his dominance over the middle Euphrates, kept up a military alliance with Elam, and fought Babylon more than once. After his defeat here he carried off the god of his city and the treasure of the royal house and withdrew north to Khazban, generally placed in the upper Habur region, its site still unidentified. The priests and scribes of Larsa were killed or taken captive when the city fell, and the population was broken up and redistributed. On Hammurabi's side, beyond the royal scribes, no name can be given with any confidence, and that in itself shows how nearly all the evidence for this war comes from the clay tablets left behind by the victors.
kits: 先要分清一件事：卡面上的這把埃及長矛（Egyptian spear，約公元前3200年，屬早王朝時期）並沒有出現在美索不達米亞的戰場上。它是早王朝埃及用來守城垣的青銅矛，矛頭以綁紮或套接的方式固定在木杆上，屬於「柄裝式長柄兵器」這一技術家族；把它放進拉爾薩之戰的裝備表，是因為兩河流域在同時段正走過同一條路：早王朝的蘇美爾戰爭藝術（最著名者為約公元前2600年的《烏爾王旗》）裡的步兵，幾乎人手一支矛、一面盾，矛頭同樣是銅或青銅、套在木柄上。真正出現在拉爾薩城下的，是一套古巴比倫時期的裝備：長矛為主兵器，銅或青銅矛頭以套筒安於木杆，另有短柄石鎚與銅斧用於破壞柴柵與攻城器械；遠射兵器是木弓配骨、銅、石箭鏃，近距離齊射仍是拉爾薩與巴比倫守軍的主要火力；防護以木牌、皮革與柳條盾牌為主，銅盔與皮制鱗甲只配給車兵與精銳；守城一方倚賴夯土磚城牆、引幼發拉底河水而成的護城壕與水門，進攻一方沒有可考的投石機或攻城塔，攻城依靠封門、斷糧與突入缺口。運輸與後勤靠牛車、驢隊與幼發拉底河上的船，糧食由被征服的城邦供應；馬匹在南部兩河用量極少，車兵更不普遍，軍隊骨幹是步兵。
kitsEn: One thing has to be sorted out first. The Egyptian spear on the card, dating from about 3200 BC in the Early Dynastic period, did not appear on any battlefield in Mesopotamia. It is a bronze spear of Early Dynastic Egypt, used to hold city walls, its head fixed to a wooden shaft by binding or by socket, and it belongs to that family of hafted, socketed long weapons. It is placed in the equipment table of the war for Larsa because the river lands were travelling the same road in the same period: in the Early Dynastic war art of Sumer, most famous in the Standard of Ur of about 2600 BC, the foot soldier is almost always shown with a spear in one hand and a shield in the other, the spearhead likewise of copper or bronze and socketed onto a wooden haft. What actually stood before the walls of Larsa was the equipment of the Old Babylonian period. The spear was the main arm, with copper or bronze heads socketed to wooden shafts, and there were short-hafted stone maces and copper axes for breaking brushwood and siege works. The missile weapons were wooden bows with bone, copper and stone arrowheads, and the close-range salvo remained the main firepower of the defenders on both sides. Protection consisted of wooden, leather and wicker shields, with bronze helmets and hide scale armour kept for chariot men and picked troops. The defenders relied on a mud-brick city wall, on a moat fed from the Euphrates, and on water gates; the attackers had no attested stone-thrower and no siege tower, and took the city by sealing the gates, cutting the food and driving in at a breach. Transport and supply rested on ox carts, donkey trains and the boats of the Euphrates, with grain furnished by the conquered cities. Horses were little used in the southern river lands, wheeled war chariots even less so, and the body of the army was infantry.
tactics: 這場戰爭的作戰順序，可以從《漢摩拉比編年史》與《巴比倫王表 A》的殘句裡排出骨架，細節則靠兩河的水文與地形補。第一步是北方的清障：漢摩拉比先以「底格里斯河長牆」封住北方越境通道，在幼發拉底河與底格里斯河之間的通道上與埃什努納聯軍交戰，於巴塞特基一役把聯軍打散，拉爾薩的北翼由此暴露。第二步是時機的選擇：春汛之後秋收之前的作戰季節是唯一的窗口，此時幼發拉底河與支流沙特卡爾河的水位下降，守方用來護城的引水溝渠可以涉水通過，而河運又能供應大軍的糧秣；漢摩拉比在這一窗口內自巴比倫城沿河南下，直線距離約一百八十公里，順河道行軍則要走近三百公里，約需十日至半月。第三步是野戰決勝：巴比倫軍隊在拉爾薩城郊列陣，步兵以密集縱隊向前推壓，拉爾薩與埃蘭、古提的聯軍在兩側展開，漢摩拉比集中兵力攻擊聯軍的接合部，潰散之後全力追擊，不給拉爾薩重整的機會。第四步是封鎖與圍城：巴比倫以步兵占據河道渡口與城外的道路，切斷拉爾薩與埃什努納、烏爾方向的聯繫，並靠截斷鹽與穀物的進口迫使城內耗盡存糧。第五步是破城：城門或被攻破、或因守軍崩潰而洞開，神廟遭到毀壞，城邦神像與王室財貨被掠走，辛-穆巴里特因此得以帶著神像北逃。整個過程裡最關鍵的技術動作不是攻城，而是調水：河道與堤防決定了進攻方向、行軍速度與守軍的士氣。
tacticsEn: The order of operations can be sketched from the surviving sentences of the Chronicle of Hammurabi and of Babylonian King List A, with the hydrology and the geography of the two rivers filling in the detail. The first step was clearing the north. Hammurabi shut the northern lines of approach with the Wall of the Tigris, fought the army of Eshnunna in the corridor between the Euphrates and the Tigris, and broke that coalition apart at the battle of Bassetki, which left the northern flank of Larsa uncovered. The second step was the choice of moment. The campaigning season between the spring flood and the autumn harvest was the only window, for during it the levels of the Euphrates and of its branch the Shatt al-Kar fell, the water channels that filled the moat could be waded, and river transport could still feed a great army. Within that window Hammurabi marched south from Babylon along the river, a distance of some hundred and eighty kilometres in a straight line and close to three hundred by the winding course of the Euphrates, a march of ten days to a fortnight. The third step was a decision in the open field. The Babylonians deployed outside Larsa, the infantry pressing forward in dense columns, while the army of Larsa with its Elamite and Gutian allies deployed to the flanks; Hammurabi concentrated on the junction of the allied line, and once it broke he pursued without giving Larsa the chance to reform. The fourth step was the blockade and the siege. Babylonian infantry held the river crossings and the roads outside the city, cutting Larsa off from Eshnunna and from Ur, and the interception of salt and grain imports was meant to exhaust what was stored inside. The fifth step was the storming. The gates were either forced or stood open after the defenders disintegrated, the temples were wrecked, the god of the city and the treasure of the royal house were carried off, and Sin-Muballit was able to retreat north with the idol. The decisive technical action in all of this was not the assault on the walls but the management of water: the channels and the embankments decided the direction of the attack, the speed of the march and the morale of the defenders.
data: 可核對的數字分三類。第一類是文本自述：作戰被繫於漢摩拉比在位第37年，通行定年為公元前1763年，部分學者據《巴比倫王表 A》的系年改置於第30年前後，短年代學則把同一事件推到公元前1801年左右；《漢摩拉比法典》序言自述「在位第37年，他毀了拉爾薩與錫帕爾，並平定了幼發拉底河上的聚落」，這是拉爾薩陷落最直接的同期文字憑據。兵力數字則完全不可考：兩河流域的泥板從不列戰兵人數，學界只能從城邦人口與徵發比例推測，兩個城邦級的軍隊各在數千人至一萬餘人之間，多數說法認為巴比倫的投入以萬人量級計，並非傳統史書中的十萬大軍。距離可以計算：巴比倫城至拉爾薩直線約一百八十公里，沿幼發拉底河道約三百公里。第二類是考古數字：拉爾薩的遺址是今日的泰勒薩米爾土丘，位於今伊拉克希納瓦爾一帶、納西里耶以南約三十公里；1900至1901年，法國考古隊由雅克·德·摩爾岡率領為羅浮宮發掘，出土寧呼爾薩格神廟的地基與上段結構、大批楔形文字泥板與銅器殘件；今日該處只剩低矮的土台與殘存的牆基。第三類是制度數字：《漢摩拉比法典》共282條，刻在約二點二五米高的玄武岩石柱上，1901年在蘇斯出土，現藏羅浮宮；此役之後約二十餘年，法典才被頒行。月份方面，現存編年史只記「第37年」而不載月；按兩河的作戰季節推斷多落在春末夏初，本檔以三月記之，屬推估而非文獻。
dataEn: The numbers that can be checked fall into three classes. The first is what the texts say of themselves. The campaign is tied to the thirty-seventh year of Hammurabi, conventionally dated to 1763 BC; some scholars, working from the sequence of Babylonian King List A, place it nearer the thirtieth year, and the Short Chronology pushes the same event to about 1801 BC. The prologue of the Code of Hammurabi states that in the thirty-seventh year he destroyed Larsa and Sippar and subdued the settlements on the Euphrates, and that is the most direct contemporary written warrant for the fall of Larsa. Figures for troops, by contrast, cannot be checked at all: the clay tablets of Mesopotamia never list the numbers under arms, and scholars can only reason from the population of the cities and from the rate of levy, putting the two city-state armies at somewhere between a few thousand and a little over ten thousand men each, with most estimates putting the Babylonian effort in the tens of thousands rather than the hundred thousands of older storytelling. Distance can be computed: the direct distance from Babylon to Larsa is about one hundred and eighty kilometres, and about three hundred by the course of the Euphrates. The second class is archaeological. The site of Larsa is the mound of Tell al-Samir, in the Shinawar district of modern Iraq, roughly thirty kilometres south of Nasiriyah; between 1900 and 1901 a French expedition under Jacques de Morgan excavated for the Louvre, recovering the foundations and lower courses of the temple of Ninhursag, a quantity of cuneiform tablets and bronze fragments; little remains today but a low mound and traces of the wall base. The third class is institutional numbers: the Code of Hammurabi has 282 provisions, cut on a basalt stele about two and a quarter metres high, found at Susa in 1901 and now in the Louvre, and it was promulgated some twenty-odd years after this campaign. As for the month, the surviving chronicle gives only the thirty-seventh year; the campaigning season of the two rivers places the operation in late spring or early summer, and this record enters March as an estimate rather than as a document.
cause: 打起來有四層原因，層層相扣。最表層是地緣：拉爾薩卡在幼發拉底河中游的沙特卡爾河兩岸，向南控制通往波斯灣的鹽、穀物與木材通道，向北窺著巴比倫的城圈；巴比倫要打通下游與海路，就必須先把這個卡口拿下。第二層是聯盟政治：辛-穆巴里特的拉爾薩與埃蘭、古提結盟，北方的埃什努納也不願坐視巴比倫坐大，於是形成一個環繞巴比倫的包圈；漢摩拉比用在位前期的十餘年逐一拆散這個包圈，先以長牆隔斷北方，再於巴塞特基擊潰蘇巴爾圖聯軍，拉爾薩的北翼由此暴露。第三層是水與土地：拉爾薩的強大，很大程度上建立在它對幼發拉底河水量分配、鹽份沉積與灌溉渠道的壟斷上；漢摩拉比以開鑿洪水渠、疏浚河道作為國策，一旦他自己掌握下游的水與鹽的調度權，就等於抽掉拉爾薩的經濟根基。制度層面的原因同樣關鍵：早王朝與烏爾第三王朝留下的是中央集權的傳統，而漢摩拉比面對的是一批自治城邦，這一組矛盾最終不能靠共主的名分化解，只能靠兼併來解決。所謂天命一類的說法在兩河並不像在東亞那樣系統化，驅動力更多是物質的：地、鹽、水與商路。
causeEn: There are four layers of cause, each resting on the one below. The surface layer is geography. Larsa sat astride the Shatt al-Kar in the middle Euphrates, controlling to the south the salt, the grain and the timber road that ran on towards the Persian Gulf, and looking north at the ring of Babylon's cities; to open the lower river and the sea road, Babylon had first to take that choke point. The second layer is alliance politics. Larsa under Sin-Muballit was allied with Elam and the Gutians, and Eshnunna in the north was unwilling to see Babylon grow strong either, so a ring formed around the Babylonian state. For the first ten-odd years of his reign Hammurabi took that ring apart piece by piece: first the wall shut off the north, then the defeat of the Subartu coalition at Bassetki opened Larsa's northern flank. The third layer is water and land. The strength of Larsa rested in large part on its control of the distribution of the Euphrates' volume, of the deposition of salt and of the irrigation channels, and Hammurabi made the cutting of flood channels and the dredging of the river a policy of state; once he held the right to allocate the water and the salt of the lower river, the economic foundation was pulled out from under Larsa. The institutional layer matters just as much. The early dynastic and Third Dynasty periods had left a tradition of centralisation, while Hammurabi was facing a set of self-governing cities, and that contradiction could not finally be dissolved by the fiction of a common lord; it could only be solved by annexation. Reasoning framed in the language of a Mandate from Heaven was nowhere near as systematic in Mesopotamia as it was in East Asia, and the driving forces here were mostly material: land, salt, water and the lines of trade.
impact: 拉爾薩陷落是南部美索不達米亞政治地圖上一次不可逆的改寫。第一，城市作為城邦國家的生命終止。城牆被拆，神廟被毀，辛-穆巴里特帶走的城邦神像使札巴巴的祭祀中斷數代；居民被拆散遷往巴比倫與其他城鎮，戰俘被賜予土地安置，這套做法成為後來亞卡德、烏爾第三王朝以及古巴比倫各代國王處理被征服城市的標準程序。第二，幼發拉底河中游的航運與鹽糧貿易被巴比倫握在手中，兩河流域下游第一次出現一個能號令整個南部平原的政權；此後漢摩拉比逐一接收伊辛、蘇普拉庫姆等城，於是有了編纂一部統一法典的行政基礎，《漢摩拉比法典》282條的頒行（一般定於公元前1750年前後）正是這一整合的制度化表現。第三，水利國策成為古巴比倫的傳統，河道整治、鹽業調度與鄉村登記制度讓美索不達米亞進入國家形成期，馬里信件所反映的行政網絡密度遠高於此前任何一個城邦時代。第四，考古上，拉爾薩遺址把早王朝的城邑形制、古巴比倫時期的城市結構與神廟經濟連成一條可考察的線索，寧呼爾薩格神廟的地基、楔形文字泥板與城防的走向，是今天復原這場戰爭的物質證據。第五，從更長的歷史看，蘇美爾城邦並立的時代就此結束，王與城邦領袖之間那種共治的關係，被一君制的中央集權取代，兩河流域此後的歷史，改由王權與神廟之間的張力來推動。
impactEn: The fall of Larsa rewrote the political map of southern Mesopotamia in a way that could not be undone. First, the life of the city as a city-state ended. The walls were broken down, the temples were wrecked, and the removal of the city's god by Sin-Muballit interrupted the cult of Zababa for several generations. The population was broken up and moved to Babylon and to other towns, and prisoners of war were given land on which to settle; the practice became the standard way in which the kings of Akkad, of the Third Dynasty of Ur and of the Old Babylonian line treated cities they had conquered. Second, the shipping of the middle Euphrates and the trade in salt and grain passed into Babylonian hands, and for the first time a single authority could give orders across the whole southern plain. Hammurabi then took Isin and Suprakum and others in turn, which gave him the administrative basis for compiling a single code, and the promulgation of the 282 provisions of the Code of Hammurabi, generally dated to about 1750 BC, is the institutional form of that integration. Third, hydraulic policy became a permanent feature of Old Babylonian government: the regulation of the river channels, the regulation of the salt trade and the registration of the countryside carried Mesopotamia into the period of state formation, and the density of administration visible in the Mari letters is far greater than anything in the city-state age. Fourth, archaeologically, the site of Larsa joins the forms of the Early Dynastic city, the urban structure of the Old Babylonian period and the temple economy into a single line of enquiry; the foundations of the temple of Ninhursag, the cuneiform tablets and the line of the fortifications are the physical evidence by which this war can now be reconstructed. Fifth, in the longer run, the age of the parallel Sumerian city-states was over, the working relationship between kings and the leading men of the cities gave way to a centralised monarchy, and the history of the river lands from then on was driven by the tension between royal power and the temples.
result: 公元前1763年（或按另一些系年前推數年），拉爾薩陷落。編年史的記載相當簡短：漢摩拉比擊敗拉爾薩的軍隊，辛-穆巴里特帶著城邦神像退往北方的哈茲班，拉爾薩城被毀，國王的像被帶走；同一記載還提到同年錫帕爾也遭毀滅，那座城在幼發拉底河東岸、靠近後來的亞述，與拉爾薩構成巴比倫南征的兩個支點。結果可以分三層講。軍事上，這是一場決定性而不是消耗性的勝利：巴比倫的攻勢一旦拿下拉爾薩，就再沒有南面戰線的牽制，辛-穆巴里特的聯盟在幾年內解體，拉爾薩作為城邦不再復原。經濟上，中游的鹽、穀物與河道調度權歸入巴比倫，漢摩拉比得以用這份收入供養一支常備步兵與龐大的工程役夫，並在十餘年內完成《漢摩拉比法典》的編纂，於公元前1750年前後頒行，把此前各城邦各自為政的慣例收攝為一套可以覆蓋整個王國的成文規則。制度上，蘇美爾城邦並立的時代告終，兩河流域的主導權在接下來近半個世紀裡集中在巴比倫，直到亞述崛起。戰術層面的評價則很節制：雙方在技術裝備、戰術思想與通信方式上差距有限，決定勝負的是河水、聯盟與政治士氣；正因如此，這場戰役在軍事史上真正的分量，在於它示範了早期國家如何靠一次兼併，把原本鬆散的區域聯盟改造成可持續的中央集權。
resultEn: In 1763 BC, or a few years earlier according to the other chronological systems, Larsa fell. The chronicle is brief: Hammurabi defeated the army of Larsa, Sin-Muballit carried off the god of his city and withdrew north to Khazban, the city of Larsa was destroyed and the king's image was taken away. The same record adds that Sippar was destroyed in the same year, that city standing on the east bank of the Euphrates near the later Assyria, and forming with Larsa the two pivots of the Babylonian advance to the south. The result can be read on three levels. Militarily it was a decisive victory rather than one of attrition: once the Babylonian offensive had taken Larsa there was no longer any southern front to pin the army down, the alliance of Sin-Muballit came apart within a few years, and Larsa was never restored as a city-state. Economically the salt, the grain and the right to regulate the channels of the middle Euphrates passed to Babylon. Hammurabi could support a standing infantry and a great number of labourers on the engineering works with that revenue, and within a dozen years he completed the compilation of the Code of Hammurabi, promulgated about 1750 BC, which gathered the separate usages of the several cities into a written rule that could cover the whole kingdom. Institutionally, the age of the parallel Sumerian city-states was over, and the leadership of the river lands stayed concentrated at Babylon for nearly half a century, until Assyria rose in its turn. The tactical verdict has to be modest: the two sides were separated by little in technical equipment, in tactical thought and in the means of communication, and what decided the outcome was the river, the alliances and political morale. Precisely for that reason the real weight of this campaign in military history lies in the demonstration it gives of how an early state used a single annexation to turn a loose regional league into a durable central power.
